correctness.rationale: The convex hull is defined by 24 explicit points of Q(sqrt(2)); exact enumeration of all 2024 triples reconstructs 26 supporting facets, 48 edges and their outward normal incidences. The face-sign criterion is necessary and sufficient at every generic orthographic direction. The symmetry generators are verified exactly; all facet-change lines in the fundamental wedge are exhausted by eight affine functions. Five exact intersection levels divide it into 54 sign cells, each checked by exact Q(sqrt(2)) comparisons; no interior sign changes remain. Spherical Jacobian and two-triangle solid-angle formulas integrate every count region into finite arctangent expressions. Dihedral-normal angle multiplicities give an independent mean check, and 1800 independent projected convex hulls corroborate the directional law. Numerical samples are not used as continuum proof.

The related regular rhombicuboctahedral distribution and the snub-cube distribution do not imply the J37 law, because local facet types/mean do not determine their global spherical sign-cell areas. This is an originality assessment relative to inspected literature and indexed records, not a proof of historical priority.

value.rationale: A canonical, historically confusing pair of polyhedra has identical face types, local vertex figures, and two exterior dihedral-angle multiplicities; both therefore have exactly equal mean silhouette complexity. Nevertheless, the twisted member has a strictly positive eleven-vertex shadow probability while the uniform member has only even-sided generic shadows. The theorem gives a full nontrivial angular law and complete directional inequalities for this natural metric-combinatorial observable, which is not a routine symmetry-axis count or generic table recomputation.
